title: 10 best quoting apps for small contractors for 2026
summary: Compare 10 quoting apps for small contractors by features, pricing, and trade fit. Find tools to send professional quotes, follow up, and collect deposits.
body_markdown:
The best quoting app for small contractors depends on how you sell your work. A solo contractor sending estimates from their truck needs fewer bells and whistles than a larger shop with office staff.


- **Topline Pro** is the best for growing home-service businesses that want to build professional quotes fast and keep leads and payments in one place.
- **Joist** is a go-to for remodelers and general contractors who want to set up milestone payments for longer projects or issue change orders as projects evolve.
- **Jobber** can work for larger service businesses that want quoting software but also need scheduling, dispatching, and tools for analyzing business performance.


Here’s a breakdown of the 10 best quoting apps for small contractors, what each one does well, what it costs, and what kind of business it fits best.

## What small contractors need from a quoting app


A quoting app helps you price a job, send the customer a clear breakdown of those costs for their approval, and then turn that quote into an invoice at the end of the job.


Small contractors need a quoting app that is:


- **Mobile-first** so you can build the estimate on your phone
- **Fast** so you can create quotes quickly and win more bids
- **Properly formatted** with scope, line items, how long the bid is good for, how much you need up front, photos that visually describe the project, and a place for customers to e-sign
- **Easily accessible** so customers can open the quote on their phone, e-sign it, and pay a deposit straight from a link without downloading an app
- **Transitions smoothly to invoicing** so you don’t have to hop into a different app to get paid


## 10 quoting apps for small contractors to consider


Below, we give you everything you need to compare our 10 favorite quoting apps by what they cost, how they help you build and send estimates, and which types of contractors they suit best.


### 1. Topline Pro


**Best for: Growing businesses that want help winning work, not just writing quotes**


Topline Pro’s quoting tool helps you get an estimate in front of a lead fast without having to sit in front of a computer.


Once the lead is in your pipeline, Sidekick (Topline Pro’s AI tool) takes the scope and pricing you give it and turns that information into a professional, branded quote.


From there, you can edit the proposal straight from your phone and send it by text or email.


After the quote goes out, Topline Pro automatically tracks whether the opportunity is pending, accepted, or declined. It also follows up on your behalf.


For bigger jobs, you can also add deposits and milestone payments. The system automatically turns those milestones into invoices as you work through the job.


Quoting is only one piece of Topline Pro. The platform also helps you bring in leads through your website, social media, and its unique Prospect Feed. Prospect Feed automatically pulls information from NextDoor when it sees people looking for the kinds of services you offer.


You can also manage customers, schedule appointments, collect reviews from happy customers, and turn your best-looking projects into Showcase pages on your website.


#### Key features


- Sidekick learns your usual line items and rates from past quotes and invoices
- Create branded quotes from rough job notes made by voice or text
- Get alerts when customers open or accept quotes
- Mobile-friendly quotes with built-in e-signatures
- Set up deposits, milestone payments
- Quote history is tied directly to the customer record


#### Pricing


Topline Pro starts at $249 per month when billed annually.


### 2. Joist


**Best for: General contractors working jobs where the scope and price can change day to day**


With Joist, you can break an estimate into sections, add detailed line items, set your markups, and then send the whole thing from your phone. This setup is great for project contractors who often need more than a one-page price quote because they’re dealing with longer, multi-stage jobs.


Customers can open the estimate on any device, review the scope, and sign it right from their phone. Joist tells you when they open or approve it. If you’re worried about an old price hanging around, especially in a volatile market for raw materials, you can set an expiration date for the quote.


Joist also makes it easy to issue change orders when homeowners add work or change their mind about materials halfway through the project. All that information stays with the same project, so you don’t have to rely on a handshake deal or scroll through a long text thread to see what you agreed to.


For bigger jobs, you can also put homeowner financing directly on the estimate through Acorn Finance, which gives customers access to 30+ lenders and loans up to $100,000. Joist separately offers contractor financing through Fundbox, plus receipt scanning and job-linked expenses to help keep project costs organized once work starts.


#### Key features


- Change orders let you document added or removed work as projects evolve
- Use deposits and milestone payments to bill in stages
- Homeowner financing from 30+ lenders through Acorn
- Contractor lending for materials, payroll, and other working capital needs
- Receipt scanning


#### Pricing


Joist starts at $8.34 per month, billed annually.


### 3. Jobber


**Best for: Service businesses like lawn care and cleaners that quote the same kind of jobs over and over**


Jobber is a full field-service platform that handles scheduling, dispatching, and more for the contracting industry. Its quoting tools are handy for operators who dish out the same handful of services, like lawn care or cleaning, to a regular roster of customers.


Operators can set up reusable templates that include pre-filled line items, pricing, and terms. If someone on your team is quoting from the field, they can pull up the right template in the mobile app, adjust the quantities or add-ons, and send it.


Jobber can also get a head start on leads that come in online.


When a customer submits a request, the AI can use what they asked for, along with your saved templates and past quotes, to build a draft for your office to review.


If that draft comes in above your usual quote value, Jobber can also flag it as a high-value opportunity, so your team knows to prioritize it. Once the quote goes out, automated follow-ups can keep after the customer if they don’t respond.


#### Key features


- Reusable quote templates
- AI-drafted quotes based on past estimates and invoices
- High-value quote alerts
- Customize quotes with branding, photos, customer reviews, and other attachments


#### Pricing


Jobber starts at $29 per month, billed annually, for one user on its Core plan. Costs scale from there based on how many people need to use the platform and which tier you’re interested in.


### 4. Housecall Pro


**Best for: HVAC, electric, and other high-ticket trades that sell good-better-best options**


Housecall Pro has a Sales Proposal tool that lets you build different packages and put each estimate side by side for easy comparison. An HVAC tech could offer various combinations of equipment and warranty lengths, then walk the homeowner through those options right on their phone or tablet.


You can add photos and descriptions to each package, pull pricing directly from Housecall Pro’s pricebook, and send the proposal by text or email to give the lead time to consider your bid.


Housecall Pro’s Pipeline tool tracks those open estimates and can automatically nudge leads by text or email if the customer hasn’t responded. Its Smart Recommendations can even adjust the timing of those follow-ups based on things like your industry and seasonality.


Housecall Pro is likely more than you need if all you’re looking for is a straightforward way to build estimates and get paid. Watch the plan tiers if quoting is your main reason for signing up.


#### Key features


- Good-better-best Sales Proposal Tool
- Prebuilt proposal templates for common services
- Wisetack customer financing
- Industry-specific pricebooks


#### Pricing


Housecall Pro plans start at $59 per month, billed annually for one user. The Essentials plan is for up to five users, and the Max includes up to eight users.


### 5. SimplyWise


**Best for: Remodelers and finish trades that want to measure, price, and visualize a job from their phone**


One SimplyWise subscription gives you access to its estimating, room scanning, visualization, receipt scanning, and mileage tools from the same app.


Take a photo in the app, describe the project by voice, or scan the room, and the Cost Estimator builds an itemized estimate in about the same time it takes you to say, “Rip out the old vanity and replace it with a new one.”


The Room Scan is especially useful for painters, cabinet makers, and remodelers. On supported devices, you can use LiDAR to measure a room and create a 3D model you can build an estimate from instead of measuring every dimension by hand.


Then there’s the Visualizer, which lets you take a photo of the existing space and generate a rendering of what the finished job could look like. That’s a much better way to get a homeowner on board with your bid than talking them through a spreadsheet of line items that adds up to an eye-popping figure.


SimplyWise offers lots of slick ways to gather the info you need to build an estimate. But if you need scheduling, dispatching, crew management, or other field services, you’ll need to choose a different tool.


#### Key features


- Generate estimates from photos, voice notes, renderings, or room scans
- Measure spaces and create 3D models with your smartphone
- Visualizer shows homeowners what the finished project will look like
- Receipt scanning
- Mileage tracking


#### Pricing


SimplyWise costs $20 per month, when billed annually.


### 6. Contractor+


**Best for: Operators who want current, local labor and material pricing built into their estimates**


Contractor+ has a deep set of tools to help you build accurate quotes.


First, you upload jobsite photos, blueprints, even competing quotes into its AI estimating tool, Estimatic. Estimatic breaks all that information into labor and materials. It uses your zip code to pull local labor rates based on BLS data and prices your materials at nearby hardware stores like Lowe’s, Home Depot, and Ace Hardware.


Once you’ve got your estimate, Contractor+ puts together a professional, branded quote to send to your prospective client.


If the cost of your services swings wildly with the price of raw goods, this is a great tool for protecting your margin. Contractors who rarely buy materials or who largely rely on their own labor to get the job done may not need all these features.


#### Key features


- Estimatic AI builds estimates from job descriptions, photos, blueprints, and other uploaded files
- Live material pricing from Lowe’s, Home Depot, and other hardware stores
- Local labor rates based on BLS data
- Shopping lists built directly from the estimates


#### Pricing


Contractor+ offers a free plan limited to five estimates per month. Its cheapest paid tier is Pro, which includes one user for $29 per month, billed annually. You’ll need to upgrade to its $500 per month Max plan for unlimited users.


### 7. QuoteIQ


**Best for: Roofers, landscapers, and other exterior trades that want to quote properties without driving out to measure them**


As the name implies, QuoteIQ is hyper-focused on quoting. Its standout feature is MapMeasure Pro.


All you have to do is type in the property address, and QuoteIQ pulls up a satellite image of the jobsite. You can then let its AI tool trace the area automatically or draw a boundary yourself. Quote IQ gives you the square footage and perimeter of that area. If you are measuring a roof, it will even tell you the angle of the pitch.


Once you have those measurements, put those in QuoteIQ’s estimating tool, and its AI can build an estimate and send it to the client.


If you are onsite, use QuoteIQ Cam to take photos, then add annotated photos, inspection forms, and other job information to your estimate.


Remote measurements aren’t a perfect replacement for an in-person look at a property, of course. Trees, additions, and other odd quirks can still throw QuoteIQ off. But it’s great for trades that spend a lot of unpaid time driving around just to measure properties.


#### Key features


- MapMeasure Pro lets you measure exterior parts of the property
- Historical aerial imagery lets you see how a property has changed over time
- QuoteIQ Cam for attaching inspection forms and annotated photos to job estimates
- InstaQuote lets homeowners request services right from your website


#### Pricing


QuoteIQ’s plans start at $25 per month, billed annually, for one user. Its Max plan comes in at $583.33 for 20 users.


### 8. Square Invoices


**Best for: Small service businesses that already use Square to get paid**


Square Invoices makes the most sense if you’re already using Square for card payments and you’d rather not add a separate app to your life.


You can send estimates by text or email, then keep that information alongside the contract, invoices, and other documentation under a single customer profile.


In higher-tier plans, Square lets you request a deposit and set up milestone payments.


Keep in mind that Square is general small-business software. You won’t get trade-specific price books or things like dispatching tools, like the more full-featured tools on this list.


#### Key features


- Keep estimates, contracts, and invoices in a single project workspace
- Set up deposits and milestone payments
- Create multi-package estimates for comparison
- Convert estimates straight to invoices
- Contract templates complete with e-signatures


#### Pricing


Square Invoices offers a free plan. Its paid tiers start at $49 per month.


### 9. QuickBooks


**Best for: Contractors who already use QuickBooks and want estimates to tie directly to their accounting software**


QuickBooks is known as accounting software first and foremost. But it also offers some quoting and estimating tools that can be handy for contractors who already use QuickBooks and want to keep things simple.


Its proposal builder lets you add your branding, attach photos, and send it to the customer for their e-signature. Once the customer accepts, QuickBooks automatically turns that estimate into an invoice.


On higher tiers, QuickBooks lets you track things like income, labor, and expenses of a project so you can track profitability.


If you’re looking for tools to help you with business development, its Customer Hub includes lead tracking with kanban boards, and you can also set appointments with clients.


If you need live pricing, dispatching, satellite measurements, or good-better-best proposal templates, QuickBooks is going to come up short. But for those who want to keep it simple and are already comfortable in QuickBooks, this is a lightweight option.


#### Key features


- E-signatures built into estimates and proposals
- Status tracking for estimates as they are viewed and accepted
- Project profitability tracking
- Opportunity tracking through Customer Hub


#### Pricing


QuickBooks Online Simple Start costs $38 per month and includes just one user. QuickBooks frequently runs introductory discounts, so the signup price may be lower.


### 10. Clear Estimates


**Best for: Residential remodelers who don’t want to build their own pricebook from scratch**


Clear Estimates comes preloaded with more than 13,000 line items and more than 400 project templates that help residential remodelers make quoting much more plug-and-play.


The material and labor pricing is all adjusted to your local market, and Clear Estimates updates that data quarterly.


Clear Estimates offers several ways to build quotes. You can describe your project, just like you'd explain it to a client, and the AI Scope Assistant will search the pricing database and put an estimate together for you. Or, you can pick a project template, say for a bathroom remodel, enter your measurements, then Clear Estimates fills in the rest. Either way, you can go back and change any line item, add your logo, contract terms, and an e-signature before sending the quote out.


Clear Estimates is a specialist tool for quotes. It explicitly states that it is not for scheduling, project management, or dispatching. If you want those tools, it does offer an integration with Buildertrend.


Contractors who run short service calls all day will do better with a different tool, but if you spend a lot of time building detailed residential remodeling bids, Clear Estimates could give you a bunch of time back.


#### Key features


- 13,000+ prepriced labor and material line items
- 400+ residential remodeling templates
- Local labor and material costs updated quarterly
- AI Scope Assistant that builds estimates from a written project description
- Blueprint, plan, drawing, and jobsite photo uploads on Pro
- Prewritten scope and contract language for customer proposals


#### Pricing


Clear Estimates starts at $59 per month, billed annually, for its Standard plan.


## How to send a quote from your phone in minutes


Here’s how you can use Topline Pro to create and send a quote from your phone in about 90 seconds.


1. Hit Create Quote.
2. Type a description of what you want in plain language. For example, “create a quote for Jake for landscaping for $200.”
3. Sidekick will check your contacts and see if there is information for Jake; otherwise, you can add those details.
4. Feel free to add more scope details if you’d like. Otherwise, the quote is now ready to send.
5. You can send by text or email. You’re welcome to add a personal note or send it over as is.
